title: Is Expired Air Carbon Monoxide Testing Effective for Screening of Cigarette Use in Orthopaedic Patients?
author: Sean Sterrenberg
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.7crhiv6

steps.title: Obtain consent and enroll patient
steps.instruction: A study team member obtains written informed consent from the patient and records enrollment in the study database.

steps.title: Administer Tobacco Use Questionnaire
steps.instruction: Provide the patient with the Tobacco Use Questionnaire and have them answer all items, including smoking status in the past 3 months, frequency, timing of last cigarette, daily consumption, quit date, second‑hand smoke exposure, other nicotine products, other smoked substances, and history of lung or breathing disease.

substeps.instruction: 1. Have the patient indicate Yes/No to “Have you smoked cigarettes in the past 3 months?”.
a. Frequency of smoking: Daily, Weekly (intermittently), Monthly (intermittently), Yearly (rarely).
b. When was your last cigarette? Today, In the last 1‑2 days, In the past week, In the past month.
c. Number of cigarettes per day: 1‑4 per day, 10 years (note: original text appears to contain a typo; retain as written).
d. How long ago did you quit smoking? I’ve never smoked, 5 years (retain options as written).
e. Exposure to second‑hand smoke: Yes, No.
f. Use of other nicotine forms: Nicotine replacement therapy (gum, patches), Cigars (if used greater than weekly), Other tobacco products (chewing tobacco), None.
g. Use of other smoked products: Marijuana, Cigars, E‑cigarettes, None.
h. History of lung or breathing disease: COPD, Asthma, Obstructive sleep apnea, Other (specify), None.

steps.title: Collect blood for nicotine/cotinine assays (Visit 1)
steps.instruction: Nursing staff performs venipuncture, draws a blood sample, orders serum nicotine and serum cotinine assays, and sends the specimen to the laboratory; results are automatically recorded in the electronic medical record.

steps.title: First Smokerlyzer breath test (Visit 1)
steps.instruction: Instruct the patient to use the Smokerlyzer® Micro EC50 device following the manufacturer’s steps 1‑15, with the breath‑hold preset to 6 seconds; record the carbon‑monoxide result in the medical record.

steps.title: Collect blood for nicotine/cotinine assays (Visit 2)
steps.instruction: During the pre‑operative visit (within 4 weeks of surgery), nursing staff repeats venipuncture, draws a blood sample, orders serum nicotine and serum cotinine assays, and sends the specimen to the laboratory; results are automatically recorded in the electronic medical record.

steps.title: Second Smokerlyzer breath test (Visit 2)
steps.instruction: Instruct the patient to perform a second breath test with the Smokerlyzer® Micro EC50 device, again following manufacturer steps 1‑15 and using a 6‑second breath‑hold; record the result in the medical record.

steps.title: Third Smokerlyzer breath test (Visit 3)
steps.instruction: On the day of surgery, peri‑operative nursing staff conducts a third carbon‑monoxide test using the Smokerlyzer® Micro EC50 device, following manufacturer steps 1‑15 with a 6‑second breath‑hold; record the result in the medical record but keep it blinded to the surgeon until after the operation.
